title: Revit View Standards and Template Use
purpose: Apply governed Revit view naming, view templates, visibility/filter controls, phasing, design-option display, and view-purpose settings consistently while keeping unresolved office-specific template names and project-specific phase/option structures noncanonical.
preconditions: The project's governing view/naming rules and approved view templates are available.
Project phase, phase-filter intent, intended view purpose, and any applicable design-option state are known.

steps.name: Name the view for governed purpose
actions: Assign a name that identifies the view type, scope/location, discipline where applicable, and purpose using the governing naming rules.
Do not adopt source example view names as canonical unless they are present in the governed naming registry.
validation: View names are consistent, searchable, and aligned to the governing S4 naming structures.
No duplicate or ad-hoc naming convention is introduced.

steps.name: Apply the approved view template
actions: Apply the approved view template for the view's purpose and type.
Use template-controlled category visibility, filters, linked-model visibility, phase/phase filter, design-option visibility, detail level, and visual style where governed.
If a recurring exception is required, route it into template governance instead of accumulating per-view overrides.
validation: The expected view template is applied where required.
Temporary or unexplained per-view overrides are absent or recorded as governed exceptions.

steps.name: Verify purpose-specific display state
actions: Confirm detail level and visual style match the view's intended use.
Confirm phase and phase filter align with project requirements and the declared view purpose.
Where Design Options are in use, confirm the view inherits the governed primary option unless an explicit By View or named-option exception is required for the declared purpose.
Confirm linked-model visibility and filter behavior are controlled through governed view/template logic rather than ad-hoc settings.
validation: The view state is consistent with its governed purpose and template.
Phase graphics represent the project phase intent without undocumented local drift.
Design-option visibility is either inherited from the governed project state or traceable to an explicit view-specific purpose.
The view can be used for its intended documentation, coordination, or export function without undocumented graphics drift.

steps.name: Record project-specific phase and option departures
actions: Treat phase names, phase sequences, phase-filter definitions, option-set names, option names, and primary-option selections as project-specific governed data unless separately approved as reusable configuration.
Record any view-specific departure from the governed phase or design-option display basis with its rationale and approval trace.
validation: No source example phase name, filter name, option name, or primary-option choice has silently become an enterprise default.

outputs: Governed Revit views with consistent naming and template-controlled graphics
evidence: View schedule or API inventory of names and applied templates
View Phase and Phase Filter inventory
Design Option visibility inventory where applicable
future_dependencies: Complete view-purpose vocabulary where not already governed
governance_notes: Exact source-era view-template names and example view names are TODO/example content and are not promoted.
Source example phase names and phase-filter combinations are implementation examples, not enterprise phase taxonomy.
Default primary Design Options per discipline are explicitly unresolved in the source and remain project-specific until separately governed.
Category-level graphics authority remains with governed Object Styles/graphics structures; views implement scoped display behavior.

provenance.migration_note: Round 005 expands the existing L6 view instruction with explicit project-bound phasing and Design Option controls while leaving source example phase names, filters, and unresolved primary-option defaults noncanonical.
